text:
Marathon Petroleum stock jumped nearly 18% over two weeks and rose another 0.02% today, riding a sharp spike in oil prices driven by geopolitical tension and supply disruptions. Oil prices have climbed as Iran-backed attacks on tankers and Saudi infrastructure threaten global supply routes, while Hurricane Isaias is disrupting U.S. Gulf of Mexico production and threatening refineries. For a refiner like Marathon, this creates a profitable squeeze: crude oil costs more to buy, but the company can pass higher prices to customers and benefits from tighter fuel markets, especially when U.S. refinery utilization is running at 92.7%—well above historical lows.

The tension has escalated sharply this week as the Trump administration has imposed additional sanctions on Iran's tanker fleet and signaled possible large-scale military operations, pushing crude from under $86 a barrel just days ago to over $96 today while global oil hit $125. When refining margins widen because crude is constrained and fuel is scarce, refiners' profits typically expand—though today's tiny move suggests the market may be pausing after yesterday's big 4.8% rally as investors wait to see how the geopolitical situation unfolds.
